highlights: Ski-in Alpine glamour with slope views, private-house interiors and restorative Asaya wellness
description:
Rosewood Courchevel Le Jardin Alpin sits at the top of Courchevel 1850, in the Jardin Alpin enclave of the French Alps, with direct access to the piste and the ski terrain of Les Trois Vallées. The address places the resort above one of Europe’s most polished winter villages, close to designer boutiques, chalet-lined lanes, high-altitude terraces and the lift network that links Courchevel with Méribel and Val Thorens. Its immediate surroundings are pure mountain theatre: groomed runs, forested ridges, crisp winter light and après-ski terraces.

Opened for the 2025/26 winter season, the hotel is Rosewood’s first ski resort and brings a deliberately residential spirit to the slopes. French designer Tristan Auer shaped the interiors around the glamour of Courchevel’s 1960s golden age: warm Alpine timber, velvet, marble, mirror and copper details, with terraces and large windows drawing the mountain views indoors. The 51 rooms and suites include generous family-friendly layouts and three signature houses, giving the property the feel of a private chalet rather than a conventional resort.

Dining gathers around SALTO, an evening restaurant inspired by the cooking of the northern Italian Alps, and SALTO Lounge, where lunch and après-ski unfold by the fireplace with slope views and a livelier evening mood. In-room dining extends the alpine theme with local and international dishes, useful after late arrivals or long snow days.

Asaya anchors the wellness offering with a 17-metre indoor pool, five treatment rooms, a treatment suite with hot tub, saunas, steam rooms, cold plunge and a children’s cavern. A Technogym fitness suite, family-friendly spaces and dedicated ski butlers add practical ease before and after days on the mountain.

highlights: Storied Tuscan estate with Brunello vines, private golf and two-star dining
description:
Rosewood Castiglion del Bosco unfolds across a 5,000-acre private estate in the Val d’Orcia, just outside Montalcino, where Brunello vineyards, cypress-lined lanes and soft Sienese hills form a protected Tuscan landscape. The property is centred on an ancient borgo with a church, castle ruins and stone lanes, placing the wine towns of Montalcino, Pienza and Siena within easy reach while keeping the mood wholly pastoral. The scale of the estate makes vineyard drives and quiet morning walks feel part of the stay.

The resort’s 42 suites occupy restored medieval farmhouses around the village, blending exposed beams, terracotta floors and country-house elegance with large terraces or garden outlooks. Eleven villas, many adapted from 17th- and 18th-century farmhouses, spread across the estate with private pools and expansive living spaces, creating a more secluded version of Tuscan life among olive groves and vineyards.

Food and wine define the rhythm here. Two-Michelin-starred Ristorante Campo del Drago serves chef Matteo Temperini’s contemporary Tuscan cooking, shaped by estate-grown produce, local suppliers and panoramic views over the Val d’Orcia. Osteria La Canonica is more informal, while La Canonica Cooking School, the Brunello winery, private tastings and the estate’s own labels deepen the culinary sense of place.

Beyond the borgo, The Club at Castiglion del Bosco is Italy’s only private golf club, set within UNESCO-listed countryside. The Spa draws on Tuscan botanicals, complemented by pools, fitness, guided biking and hiking, horseback riding and seasonal cultural experiences. The result is less a hotel inserted into Tuscany than a historic estate still living through wine, food, craft and landscape.

highlights: Baroque banking heritage reborn with Bavarian brasserie energy and serene Asaya wellness
description:
Rosewood Munich occupies a distinguished address on Kardinal-Faulhaber-Straße in Munich’s Altstadt, placing the hotel between the city’s historic core, luxury shopping streets and major cultural landmarks. The Residenz, Odeonsplatz, Frauenkirche, Marienplatz and the Bavarian State Opera are all part of the surrounding old-town fabric, making the property unusually well placed for guests moving between museums, churches, boutiques and evening performances.

The hotel brings together the former State Bank of Bavaria and the Palais Neuhaus-Preysing, translating layers of institutional and aristocratic history into a contemporary urban retreat. Its 132 rooms and suites include 59 suites and a small collection of houses, with interiors that reinterpret Bavarian craftsmanship through tailored furniture, warm woods, soft textiles and modern detailing. The mood is less grand formality than composed residential polish, with courtyards and historic façades softening the city-centre scale.

Brasserie Cuvilliés gives the hotel its main culinary stage, serving Alpine-inflected cooking with Bavarian character from breakfast through dinner. Bar Montez adds a more nocturnal pulse with cocktails and music, while the Wintergarten, Palaishof and Schanigarten create seasonal spaces for afternoon tea, terrace dining and quieter drinks. The result is a dining programme that feels distinctly Munich rather than imported.

Asaya Spa introduces Rosewood’s wellness language to the Bavarian capital, with treatment rooms, saunas, an indoor pool and fitness facilities for a complete city-spa rhythm. Meeting and event spaces support the business side of the address, but the strongest impression is cultural: a heritage building recast as a polished base for Munich’s art, opera, shopping and old-town walks.

highlights: Restored lakeside castle with Alpine views, imperial romance and rare lakeside serenity
description:
Rosewood Schloss Fuschl rises directly above Lake Fuschl in the Salzkammergut, less than half an hour from Salzburg yet wrapped in forested mountains and clear alpine water. The castle began life as a 15th-century hunting lodge for Salzburg’s prince-archbishops, and its latest restoration has returned the landmark to the lake with a more polished, quietly contemporary character. The location forms a natural bridge between Salzburg and the lakes of the Salzkammergut, making the landscape as important as the building.

The hotel has 98 rooms, suites and chalets, many oriented toward the water or the surrounding woodland. Inside, the mood balances castle romance with light Austrian craftsmanship: vaulted historic spaces, pale woods, refined textiles and windows framing the lake. The setting feels almost cinematic, yet the present atmosphere is calmer and more residential than theatrical.

Dining is spread across six venues. Schloss Restaurant draws on regional produce, while Seeterrasse and the seasonal See Club turn toward the lake. Vinothek focuses on wine, Sisi Teesalon brings afternoon tea into a heritage setting, and Schloss Bar gives the castle its evening glow. Details such as the hotel’s own bee colony and local fisherman reinforce the connection to the landscape.

Asaya Spa extends the restorative side of the resort with saunas, treatment spaces, an indoor pool, an outdoor infinity pool facing Lake Fuschl, a gym, yoga and sound-bathing sessions. E-bikes, hiking, lake access and watersports make the estate feel active as well as contemplative, while Salzburg’s baroque old town and music culture remain close enough for a refined day excursion.

highlights: Petersplatz landmark with rooftop dining, spa calm and luminous Old Town views
description:
Rosewood Vienna occupies a landmark position on Petersplatz in the Innere Stadt, Vienna’s historic first district. Peterskirche is directly part of the square’s atmosphere, while St. Stephen’s Cathedral, the Graben, Kohlmarkt, the Hofburg and the city’s museums and opera life sit within easy walking distance. The hotel’s address makes it feel woven into Vienna’s old-town rhythm rather than merely adjacent to it, with shopping, cafés and imperial architecture immediately outside.

Set within a restored 19th-century building, the hotel frames Viennese heritage through contemporary residential design. Its 99 rooms and suites include distinctive signature houses, some looking toward the old city, Peterskirche, the Hofburg or the Graben. Interiors use a composed palette, modish accents and careful craft references rather than heavy period theatre, allowing historic façades and urban views to carry much of the atmosphere.

Dining rises above the rooftops at Neue Hoheit Restaurant, where Austrian cuisine is given a modern, seasonal expression. Neue Hoheit Bar brings a livelier sixth-floor rhythm, THE1835 focuses on signature drinks and panoramic city views, and the Garden Room offers a quieter indoor-outdoor setting. Wine experiences, including vintner-led tastings and excursions into Vienna’s vineyards, add a specifically local dimension to the culinary programme.

Asaya Spa and the fitness facilities create a polished wellness counterpoint in the middle of the city, with treatments and relaxation spaces designed for retreat between museum visits, shopping and evening performances. Meetings and events are handled in elegant rooms suited to private celebrations or corporate gatherings, but the essential appeal remains the address: a contemporary Rosewood interpretation of Vienna from one of its most atmospheric squares.
